china-1931-2:p0424_1.rationale: Monthly and annual average Shanghai telegraphic transfer quotations against sterling, foreign currencies and bar silver. This is exchange-rate data; bar silver quotations are included but only as a rate column.

china-1931-2:p0425_1.rationale: Annual highest and lowest official sterling T.T. quotations from 1890 to 1931, showing exchange variation. One value is unreadable but the quantitative structure is clear.

china-1931-2:p0425_2.rationale: Annual average exchange rates of principal foreign currencies against the Haikwan tael, 1914-1930.

china-1931-2:p0425_3.rationale: Annual average T.T. rates on London against Shanghai taels, 1909-1931, in two blocks.

china-1931-2:p0426_1.rationale: Silver imports and exports (bars, sycee and coin) with net balances, compiled from Maritime Customs statistics. This is a treasure movement series, so it is primarily trade, with finance as secondary.
review_questions: Is there a need for a tag for bullion or treasure movements, especially silver? The existing silver tag is for mining and commodity content.

china-1931-2:p0427_1.rationale: Gold imports and exports (bars, dust and coin) with net movements, drawn from customs statistics. Under the rules, gold exports are trade with exports and gold.

china-1931-2:p0431_1.rationale: Graduated tax rates on the net profit of banks, set by the share of profit relative to capital. The tax is on banks.

china-1931-2:p0444_1.rationale: Old Chinese standard of capacity units with their equivalents in litres, quarts and gallons.

china-1931-2:p0444_2.rationale: New metric standard of capacity, with kung units and their decimal relations to the litre.

china-1931-2:p0444_3.rationale: Market standard of capacity units and their relations to each other and to the old sheng.
